sections.title: The letter jota
paragraphs: The letter is named (jota) /ˈʒɔtɐ/. It makes one single sound in European Portuguese. You hear it at the start of the word (jogo) /ˈʒo.ɣu/, which means game. The letter always keeps this one sound.

sections.title: Mouth and voice
paragraphs: This sound is a fricative. A fricative is a consonant where the air is pushed through a narrow gap and makes a hiss. Lift the front of your tongue just behind the ridge behind your upper teeth. Push your lips forward a little. Blow air smoothly through the gap and turn your voice on. Touch your throat to feel it shake.

sections.title: Reading the letter
paragraphs: The letter always has the same sound in all positions. You read it as /ʒ/ at the start of (janela) /ʒɐˈnɛ.lɐ/. You also read it as /ʒ/ in the word (jogo) /ˈʒo.ɣu/.

sections.title: Common mistakes
paragraphs: Do not start this sound with a hard stop like the j in English jam. That English sound begins by blocking the air completely. Instead, say the sound of the s in measure or vision. Keep the air flowing smoothly without any sudden pop.
